main_text.head: INSTITVTIONVM MEDICARVM LIBER VI, De VICTVS RATIONE.
CAP. I. De Alimento.
main_text.p: POstrema hæc est medicinæ pars, communis ægro cum sano. Ratio enim victus est necessaria non tantum ad sanitatem restituendam, sed & præsentem conservandam. Consistit autem in legitimo usu sex rerum non naturalium, sine quibus non vivitur. Res non naturales ideo dicuntur, quia nec secundum naturam humano corpori insunt, ut facultates, temperamenta; nec tamen præter naturam, ut morbus, & symptoma. sed medio modo se habent. nam si ijs bene utaris prosunt; sin minus, nocent. hujusmodi sunt aër, cibus, potus, motus,

page.notes: The first letter P is a large initial, joined to "ostrema" as printed as "Postrema". The final "tus," at the right is a catchword-like continuation of "motus," set at the line end; it is printed as a separate line and kept. Some letters in the scan are faint (e.g. "usu", "sex") and are read with reasonable confidence; no [?] marks were required. The marginal column at the far right belongs to the facing page and is not transcribed.
